## 5. Discarded walks (`ban`)

A walk origin is banned when its straight-line run falls into an illegal opcode or padding, when a branch target is itself junk, or when two decodings conflict (the weaker one is dropped).  Executed/guaranteed code is never banned.  Calls to a banned target stay code (the call bytes are valid); only the target is left out.

| origin | seed (layer, tag) | reason |
|---|---|---|
| 2A:4441 | walk origin (not a seed) | conflicting decodings: 2A:4440 vs the instruction at 2A:4441 (overlaps_instruction); the walk entered mid-instruction |
| 00:21A0 | walk origin (not a seed) | branch/seed target is junk: runs_into_padding (code flow reaches run of 00) |
| 2E:6DD0 | walk origin (not a seed) | illegal_opcode at 2E:6E45 reached by straight-line fall-through (db $FC) |
| 2E:5FA2 | walk origin (not a seed) | branch/seed target is junk: runs_into_padding (code flow reaches run of 00) |
